item.title: In 1930, a Pittsburgh plumber built an aluminium observatory that helped him meet Einstein
item.description: Established in 1930 by Leo Scanlon, the Valley View Observatory in Pittsburgh quickly gained traction among amateur astronomers, primarily due to its cost-effective construction and unique aluminium dome. Scanlon's fresh approach drew attention from enthusiasts nationwide, leading to a memorable encounter with Albert Einstein in 1934, who appreciated the spirit of amateur science. To honor its significant role in astronomy, asteroid 8131 was named 'Scanlon', recognizing the observatory's legacy.

item.title: Georgia farmer turned scrap metal into folk art, filling his yard with figures that reached museums
item.description: After stepping away from farming and preaching, Reuben Aaron Miller channeled his creativity into art. He crafted enchanting, wind-powered whirligigs and striking metal figures that captured the attention of collectors near and far. His partnership with R.E.M. propelled his art to new heights, significantly boosting its market value. Now featured in numerous museum exhibitions, Miller's work continues to resonate within the American folk-art community.

item.title: In 1956, Tressa Prisbrey turned discarded bottles into a 15-building folk-art village in California
item.description: Tressa Prisbrey, at age 60, began building Bottle Village using glass bottles from a local landfill. Over 25 years, she constructed 15 unique structures dedicated to her lost children and their memories. The site eventually became a cultural landmark and received various recognitions for its artistic significance. Visitors paid small admission fees to see her creative work and hear her story.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Alice Waters’ school garden project grew into a global network of 5,800 programmes across 75 countries
item.description: Launched back in 1995 in California, the Edible Schoolyard Project has blossomed into a global initiative founded by chef Alice Waters. The project imparts essential lessons on gardening and environmental stewardship, seamlessly integrating with subjects like science and math. With a mission to foster healthy eating habits, it has inspired educational platforms across more than 75 countries, aiming to weave food education into everyday school curricula for enhanced student wellbeing.

item.title: Australian court orders bamboo removal after roots block neighbour’s sewer, awards A$6,253 in damages
item.description: In a landmark decision, an Australian court addressed a bamboo dispute affecting two neighboring properties in New South Wales. The court determined that the bamboo created a blockage and posed a risk for future damage to the sewer line. As a result, Homes NSW was ordered to compensate A$6,253.50 for previous treatment costs. The ruling highlights the importance of communication and diligent records for homeowners facing similar issues.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Aryash Shyam, 14-year-old Indian-American who won $1,000 for a story set in 1776
item.description: Indian-American student Aryash Shyam, 14, has won a $1,000 national writing prize for his historical-fiction story set in a Philadelphia print shop on July 4, 1776. The Pennsylvania ninth-grader was among four middle-school winners of the 2026 John Estey Student Writing Competition. He has also earned recognition for projects involving space research, artificial intelligence and robotics.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scottish church turned into five-bedroom home and bistro
item.description: The Old Kirk, a former church, has undergone extensive renovations to become a family home. The property features five bedrooms and spacious living areas, combining original charm with modern elements. It currently operates as a bistro while being on the market for offers over £550,000. The home retains beautiful architectural details, including arched windows and high ceilings. Surrounding gardens provide a peaceful setting and enhance the property’s appeal.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Woman buys £15,000 diamond ring for just £5 at car boot sale
item.description: A woman found a ring at a car boot sale that cost her £5 and initially seemed ordinary. She later took the ring to a valuation event at WeBuyVintage for a professional opinion. The gemologist examined the ring, discovering it was a genuine diamond set in 18-carat gold. The estimated value of the ring was approximately £15,000, shocking the woman who bought it.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: New Zealand couple turns old school into a home with a twist
item.description: After acquiring a rundown school in Tokanui, Ian and Sue Rogers dedicated years and around NZ$250,000 to revitalize the property, successfully turning it into a beloved family residence. They maintained many of the school’s original features, which highlight its rich history. They even converted a damaged swimming pool into a delightful chalet. Eager for their next venture, the couple has decided against tackling another school renovation.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: London man bought painting for £45 in 1968; it turned out to be a Van Gogh worth up to €15 million
item.description: A painting bought for just £45 from a London junk shop in 1968 was later authenticated as an original Vincent van Gogh. The artwork, which had previously sold for only £4 at a farm sale in 1967, changed hands several times before being sold to a private collector for approximately €12 million to €15 million in 2020.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Shania Twain turns childhood hunger into school support for vulnerable children through her charity
item.description: Founded in 2010, Shania Twain's Shania Kids Can initiative seeks to empower children facing poverty and food insecurity. The program provides academic help and emotional support in a nurturing school atmosphere, aiming to enhance children's self-esteem, food security, and mental health, all vital for effective learning. With dedicated Clubhouses, the foundation directly engages with children in their everyday setting, steadily reaching out to underserved communities throughout North America.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A judge voided Rhode Island’s seizure of 31 acres planned for 252 affordable homes
item.description: A federal judge ruled against the Town of Johnston, asserting the town lacked authority to seize a property. The judge's decision allows the Santoro family to proceed with a 252-unit affordable housing project. The town had attempted to use eminent domain to halt the development, claiming the land was needed for a municipal complex. Legal challenges arose regarding the town’s adherence to proper procedures and public notification.

item.title: Cleveland must consider compensation after rezoning a $52,100 used-car lot investment for housing
item.description: An Ohio appellate court has determined that Cleveland owes TMS Enterprises compensation following a contentious zoning amendment. The firm had invested in land with plans for a used-car dealership, but the city reclassified the site from commercial to residential, derailing their business intentions. TMS argued this decision violated their property rights. The court upheld the initial judgment, initiating the steps for formal compensation proceedings.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A UK civil servant allegedly earned £349,378 across eight government jobs between 2020 and 2023
item.description: A UK civil servant allegedly earned £349,378 across eight government jobs between February 2020 and September 2023. Kashim Chowdhury, 55, reportedly held five full-time roles simultaneously and was contracted to work 183 hours a week. He is accused of fraudulently securing positions at several government departments and denies nine counts of fraud.
